decisions.reason: Changing the backend source for metadata attributes does not alter which access rights, referral identity, badges, or prize-ticket states follow an NFT after transfer.
Reading metadata attributes from a live on-chain function does not change the selected Base network or deployment scope.
The metadata attribute source does not change the royalty amount, royalty structure, NFT standard, creator controls, or marketplace policy.
The accepted change concerns the source of metadata attributes, not cover-image rendering, wallet media presentation, or contract inclusion in the dashboard.
Using live on-chain metadata attributes does not change whether an owner can locate NFTs in a wallet or dashboard.
The referral code remains the NFT token serial and its required display locations remain unchanged; the source decision only changes how metadata attributes are populated.
The metadata source change does not alter the randomness provider, on-chain winner-selection process, fairness, or applicable draws.
The accepted metadata sourcing change does not alter badge award thresholds, award basis, or on-chain attachment semantics.
The source decision does not change when mint-success feedback appears or which token identifier it displays.
No FAQ copy or FAQ topic is changed by the decision to source backend metadata attributes from the live on-chain function.
The metadata attribute source does not affect the Transak provider, payment methods, wallet provisioning, mint destination, or deferred lifecycle state.
The change to metadata attribute sourcing does not alter the NFT ebook format or unlimited edition supply.
